Content.Strong: Failure modes you should now be able to diagnose

Chapter.Content: This is the one list I want you to retain from the lesson because each symptom maps to a specific raster stage.

ListItem.Content: Exploding triangle across the screen: likely bad projection, invalid , clipping failure, NaNs or wrong coordinate convention.
Mesh shape correct but textures warp with depth: affine interpolation used where perspective-correct interpolation was required.
Hairline cracks between adjacent triangles: inconsistent edge ownership/top-left implementation, floating-point coverage disagreement or mismatched vertices.
Half-pixel shift: sample-center/viewport convention error.
Everything vertically inverted: Vulkan viewport/projection Y convention mismatch; in Kairo specifically, remember projection(1,1) *= -1.
Geometry disappears after enabling depth: wrong clear value, wrong compare operator, projection-depth convention mismatch or invalid depth range.
Distant coplanar objects flicker: depth precision/Z-fighting, often worsened by an excessively tiny near plane.
Normal map suddenly produces garbage on one triangle: UV Jacobian determinant near zero, derivative/tangent reconstruction degeneracy.
Some vertices appear to contain garbage: vertex stride/offset/format disagreement.
Large indexed mesh has surprising VS cost: poor index locality/post-transform-cache reuse.
One triangle is missing around the near plane: clipping or projection convention error rather than necessarily backface culling.
Reversed-Z attempt produces a blank frame: projection, clear value and comparison direction were not changed as one invariant.

This is not only semantic.
On tile-based architectures especially, avoiding unnecessary attachment preservation can save memory traffic.
At the end of the pass, you similarly decide:
Chapter.Code: STORE DONT_CARE
Chapter.Content: STORE means later work needs the generated contents.
DONT_CARE means the attachment can be discarded after its current purpose has been fulfilled.
This is one of the simplest places where knowing future resource lifetime directly turns into GPU bandwidth optimization.

Depth: load = CLEAR store = DONT_CARE
Chapter.Content: Why?
Color must survive because the editor samples/presents it later.
Object ID must survive because picking can copy a pixel to a readback buffer later.
Depth only needs to participate during rasterization in that pass.
The viewport does not currently sample it later.

Content.Strong: MSAA changes the framebuffer from one sample to many

Chapter.Content: At 1×:
Chapter.Code: one pixel └── one coverage/depth/color sample
Chapter.Content: At 4× MSAA:
Chapter.Code: one pixel ├── sample 0 ├── sample 1 ├── sample 2 └── sample 3
Chapter.Content: Each sample has an exact sample location.

Rasterization tests primitive coverage against those sample positions, producing a coverage mask. Vulkan describes multisampling precisely this way: each framebuffer pixel has rasterizationSamples exact sample points, each attachment holds per-sample color/depth/stencil state, and the resulting multisampled color can later be resolved to a single-sample image. docs.vulkan.org
